newsitem.title: INDIA: India aiming for 20,000 MW nuclear power by 2020.
newsitem.headline: India aiming for 20,000 MW nuclear power by 2020.

text.p: India aims to expand nuclear power capacity to 20,000 megawatts by the year 2020, Atomic Energy Commission chairman R. Chidambaram said on Thursday.

"In building the nuclear power plant and building other parts of the nuclear fuel cycle, India should be aiming for 20,000 megawatts by the year 2020," Chidambaram told Asian News International in an interview.

"In terms of developing indegenous technology, we are among the leading countries. It is essential that India should aim for very ambitious growth in the power sector," he told the television news agency.

India has 10 operating reactors that generate about 2,000 megawatts between them. The power-starved country's demand for electricity is growing at nine percent a year and government officials say it needs to generate 142,000 megawatts by the year 2007 against the present capacity of about 83,288 megawatts.
Chidambaram said the government was considering building another four reactors with 220 megawatts capacity each.
"It is very clear that India is in desperate need of power, power of all kinds," he said.
"I am convinced that per capita electricity consumption in India must increase by a factor of eight to 10 if the poorest of us are to have a reasonable standard of living."
The atomic energy chief said a controversial government proposal to allow foreign firms to own nuclear power stations would shore up India's electricity generating capacity.
"If there is a specific proposal, certainly we will consider it," Chidambaram said. "There can be no growth without power."
He said Asian hunger for energy would drive future growth of the global nuclear power sector.

"The countries of the West have a surfeit of energy. The growth is taking place in those countries where they don't have any fossil resources. One third of Japan's and North Korea's power comes from the nuclear sector," Chidambaram said.
